ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 1, it is known that point O is on line AB, with rays OD and OC on opposite sides of line AB, and $ \angle COD=80^\circ$. Ray OE is always the bisector of $ \angle AOD$. As shown in Figure 2, let $ \angle AOD=n^\circ$. It is known that $ \angle DOE=2\angle AOC$. Find the value of $n$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that,\\
$\because OE$ bisects $\angle AOD$,\\
$\therefore \angle DOE=\frac{n^\circ}{2}$,\\
$\because \angle COD=80^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOC=80^\circ-n^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle DOE=2\angle AOC$,\\
$\therefore \frac{n}{2}=2(80-n)$,\\
$\therefore n=\boxed{64}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 1, it is known that point O is on line AB, with rays OD and OC on opposite sides of line AB, and $\angle COD=80^\circ$. Ray OE is always the bisector of $\angle AOD$. As shown in Figure 2, let $\angle AOD=n^\circ$. It is known that $\angle DOE=2\angle AOC$. Find the value of $n$.
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given that,\\ $\because OE$ bisects $\angle AOD$,\\ $\therefore \angle DOE=\frac{n^\circ}{2}$,\\ $\because \angle COD=80^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle AOC=80^\circ-n^\circ$,\\ $\because \angle DOE=2\angle AOC$,\\ $\therefore \frac{n}{2}=2(80-n)$,\\ $\therefore n=\boxed{64}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure contains multiple small figures; Figure 2 used in the problem shows A, O, B on the same horizontal straight line, with A on the left side of O and B on the right side of O; the ray OD starting from O is above the straight line AB, the ray OC is below the straight line AB, and the ray OE is between OA and OD. Therefore, in Figure 2, ∠COD crosses the ray OA on the left side, and can be divided into two parts: ∠AOD and ∠AOC. Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOD = n°, and ∠COD = 80°. Because ∠COD = ∠AOD + ∠AOC, ∠AOC = 80° − n°. Also because OE is the angle bisector of ∠AOD, ∠DOE = n°/2. The problem states that ∠DOE = 2∠AOC, therefore n/2 = 2(80 − n). Solving gives n/2 = 160 − 2n, 5n/2 = 160, so n = 64.
